messages:
mike: Started a focused benchmark run to repro the odd kernel flip we saw yesterday. Targets: A100, H100, L40S; seq lens 128/512/1024/2048; batch sizes 1/4/16/64.

sophia: Nice — did you run with and without KV prefix caching?

mike: Yeah. Two modes: cold (no KV cache) and warm (prefix cache primed with 512 tokens). Command: ```./run_attn_bench --model=redwood-compat --gpus=A100,H100,L40S --seqs=128,512,1024,2048 --bsz=1,4,16,64 --kvmode=warm,cold --repeat=30 --profile=nvprof```

ana: bench-bot posted the summary earlier but TL;DR: H100 switches from FlashV1->PagedFusion at seq 1024 for bsz>=16; latency jitter spikes on paged fusion at seq 2048 under warm KV.

kevin: Can you paste the numbers? even rough p50/p95 helps.

mike: Pasted rough table below (latency ms, p50/p95):
```
A100, seq1024, bsz16, cold: 22 / 36
A100, seq1024, bsz16, warm: 18 / 29
H100, seq1024, bsz16, cold: 19 / 33
H100, seq1024, bsz16, warm: 21 / 88  <-- big p95 jump
L40S, seq1024, bsz16, warm: 26 / 40
```

ana: That H100 warm p95 (88ms) is alarming. Any traces pointing to KV cache eviction or kernel thrash?

mike: Profile shows frequent kernel selection oscillation: runtime chooses paged fusion for steady throughput but every ~200ms we hit a fallback path that drains KV pages, then kernel selector flips back to FlashV1 for a few requests. The transition cost causes the tail latency spike. Attached a small stack-ish log: ```selector: choose=paged_fusion; fallback=flashv1; reason=kv_page_fault; reclaim=async_eviction```

bench-bot: Autodetected memory-pressure events on H100 when warm KV + bsz>=16 + seq>=1024. Paging counters: gpu_mem_pressure=0.72 -> eviction_rate increased.

sophia: So hypothesis: paged fusion keeps more KV in device memory but sometimes misses and triggers slow async eviction path that stalls a few calls. Could be kernel bug or allocator interference with other tasks.

kevin: Can we reproduce with isolated single process, no other tenants? Also try disabling async_eviction to see if fallback stays stable.

mike: Ran single-tenant isolate — still reproduced. Then ran with config flag --kv_async_eviction=false: tail p95 stabilized to ~32ms, but throughput dropped 8% for seq2048. So async_eviction buys throughput but at cost of tail.

ana: Tradeoff makes sense. For product SLOs we prefer consistent latency, so default should be conservative. But we need smarter heuristic: enable async_eviction when sustained throughput > X or when batch size > Y, and ensure a backoff window to avoid oscillation.

kevin: Agreed. Also we should add a short circuit: if kernel selector flips more than N times in M ms, temporarily pin to safer kernel for T seconds. Prevents thrash.

mike: I'll open a draft RFC with data and propose: (1) default async_eviction=false for H100 in warm-KV high-bsz regime; (2) implement flip-suppression pin; (3) add an opt-in high-throughput mode that preallocates KV pages to avoid mid-run faults.

bench-bot: Created ticket INF-4821 with link: https://redwood.internal/infra/INF-4821

ana: For immediate mitigation on hosted side, roll a canary that forces paged_fusion off for H100 when seq>=1024 and bsz>=16. Rollout window 24h.

mike: Will coordinate canary. I'll also attach perf traces (nvprof + trace events) to the ticket.

kevin: One more ask — run a quick sweep on L40S with same config but smaller batch sizes (1/4/16) — we saw different behavior previously. Could be quantization or memcpy path difference.

mike: On it. Expect results in ~2 hours. Posting logs back here when done. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

sophia: Thanks — if anyone wants to pair on the selector pin logic ping me.

kevin: cc @sre for deploying the temporary kernel flag to hosted backends.

mike: End of thread for now — will update once L40S sweep finishes and after I file the RFC.
